chunks: Yunus narrated from Abdullah ibn Muskān from Abū Baṣīr who said:

The legal penalty (ḥadd) for the Jew, the Christian, and the slave regarding wine and drinking it is the same; and the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimmah) were settled upon the condition that they may drink it in their own houses.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslim subjects living in Islamic state)
key_terms.الْفِرْيَةِ: The act of drinking or consuming the intoxicant
key_terms.حَدّ: Legal penalty or fixed punishment prescribed by Sharia

ai.seo_question: What is the legal penalty for wine consumption for non-Muslims and slaves in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani’s *al-Istibsar* clarifies that the *ḥadd* (fixed legal penalty) for intoxicants applies uniformly to Jews, Christians, and slaves, countering the view that they are exempt from corporal punishment. It further specifies that the concession for *Ahl al-Dhimmah* to consume wine is restricted to private consumption within their homes, distinguishing their status from free Muslims in public spaces. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the consistency of legal penalties across different social and religious classes regarding *khamr*.
